This commit changes the medrecord demo startup script (start-demo.sh) so the local backend is reached through a fixed, free ngrok web address instead of the previous cloudflared tunnel, which was abandoned because the named-tunnel option would have required paying for a domain. The message explains that an earlier note blaming ngrok for breaking secure connections was re-diagnosed: the real cause was ngrok's free-tier browser-warning page, which can be skipped by sending a specific request header. The script edit itself looks complete and internally consistent, and the attached activity log shows the author did start the backend, open the tunnel, and run curl tests that returned successful responses; I'm relying on those logs and the commit description here, not on anything I executed. The commit also updates internal tracking files (a file-ownership registry, a trace log, and the project-state document). No story or issue was attributed to this commit, and none is needed, since this is self-contained infrastructure work whose purpose is clear on its own. I'm marking it Pending rather than complete because the commit explicitly frames the work as two parts: the backend and script side is finished and checked via curl, but the matching frontend change (adding the same header to the app's API client in src/api/apiClient.ts) is explicitly left open and handed to another agent for the next session, with on-device re-verification still outstanding. Until that piece lands, the tunnel switch is not fully usable from the app.

It also rewires the hook configuration file to call these new scripts before and after tool calls, at session start, on each user prompt, and when a subagent stops, and adds the backing state files (agent registry, file-ownership registry, workflow state, and the audit log itself). The diff is broadly consistent with what the message describes, and the "5-phase" framing lines up with the phase labels inside the individual scripts. The new agent-gate.sh looks like its successor and the settings file is repointed to it, so the removal is probably deliberate, but because it isn't called out this is a routine traceability gap worth confirming. Separately, I only read the diff and the message here and did not run any of this, and several of the new scripts carry their own comments noting that parts are unverified or may not fire in the project's current one-session-per-agent model, so this should be treated as landed code rather than as tested behavior. This is the merge commit for PR #6, a bundle of pre-pilot fixes for the MedRecord app: the patient Visit Detail (P3) and Profile (P5) screens were moved off mock data onto real API calls, four cross-flow integration bugs (BUG-IT-1 through BUG-IT-4) were fixed and re-checked by the integration tester (the notes show 6 of 7 scenarios passing and 1 skipped), a backend guard was added so a patient's mobile number can't be changed, the OTP resend cooldown was shortened, and supporting docs, review write-ups, and a new integration-tester agent definition were updated. This is the merge of PR #6, a pre-pilot batch for the patient-facing app (tracked against story P3, which was already attributed upstream — no separate story was needed). Most of what the message and PR describe is backed by the diff: the P3 visit-detail and P5 profile screens are genuinely moved off hard-coded mock data onto real backend calls with loading and error states, the developer-only demo switcher buttons are removed, the four integration bugs are addressed in code (doctor-created patients are now registered on the server synchronously so they can log in, consent revoke now clears all matching consent records, the patient timeline and doctors-access screens are wired to real endpoints, and the SSL-pinning helper is guarded so it no longer crashes in Expo Go), and the backend now rejects any attempt to change a patient's mobile number with a 400 error. One claim does not hold up: the PR says OTP resend with a 30-second cooldown was "added" to the doctor (D1) and patient (P1) login screens, but a resend feature with a cooldown timer already existed on both screens long before this work (present since the first Doctor Visit Flow merge); what actually changed here is the cooldown constant being lowered from 45 seconds to 30. That difference between "added" and "shortened" is why I'm flagging this. I have only read the diff and the accompanying notes, not executed anything; the PR references device and integration testing passing as of merge time, but I can't confirm that from here, and several items (cert pinning validation, EAS build, doctor profile screen, account-deletion UI) are explicitly deferred to a later version rather than completed.

This commit changes the sync worker so that when a network request fails because the connection drops, it waits about 1.5 seconds and tries once more before giving up, instead of immediately marking the item as failed. That specific change looks complete and internally consistent. The problem is the commit message, which says "Fixed the sync bug" and claims "all edge cases handled now" — the diff only adds a single retry for one failure mode (a dropped connection), and the retry attempt itself is not wrapped in the same error handling, so if the second attempt also fails it would still raise an unhandled error. The "all edge cases handled" claim is broader than what the code actually shows, so I'm flagging it for a developer to reconcile the message with the change. No story or issue was attributed to this commit; given the vague "the sync bug" phrasing, it would also help to have the developer or TPM confirm which tracked item this belongs to. To be clear, I only read the message and the diff — I did not run the sync worker or test any of these paths.
